truth: LIVE — this is the method CWI actually uses, documented from real operations 2026-09-14/15.
principle: A claim is not a result. Only scan-confirmed facts are published as verified. Everything else is labeled exactly what it is.

evidence_tiers.meaning: Confirmed by independent evidence (e.g., full playlist scan finding the track at a position). Publishable as fact.
Claimed by a party but evidence contradicts or is missing. Recorded with the contradicting evidence, not deleted.
Claimed with no evidence either way yet. Held, not published as fact.
Simulated or demo data. Always labeled. Never upgraded to LIVE without fresh evidence.

rules: Never publish a promise as a placement. Scan first.
Record unverified claims WITH their contradicting evidence — the log of what failed is as valuable as the wins.
Payola-adjacent sources get flagged, not courted. (A curator selling $25 adds is a flag, not a lead.)
Metrics carry observed dates. '307,439 lifetime plays' means observed 2026-09-14, not forever.
An empty ledger is a feature: publishing zero verified placements beats publishing hoped-for ones. It can only be wrong if evidence is missing.

worked_example.situation: Two curators claimed That Boy Hi Hat playlist adds on 2026-09-14.
worked_example.what_cwi_did: Ran full playlist scans on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-15 instead of announcing the claims.
worked_example.result: New Rap Hits: 3 tracks VERIFIED at positions 21/30/31 (full 105-track scan). 'No Label Needed': track absent in two scans — UNVERIFIED. 'It's Goin': playlist unlocatable — UNVERIFIED, payola flag raised.
worked_example.lesson: The announcement went out only for the verified placement. The failed claims became intelligence, not embarrassment.

how_to_verify_any_claim: Open the target playlist in Spotify, search the track title or artist, confirm presence. Send scan evidence to hp@cumulativeweb.com to dispute or update a record.
teach_forward: Re-teach this as: a four-tier evidence system any agent or team can adopt — VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED/UNCONFIRMED/SAMPLE — with the worked playlist example. Attribution: Cumulative Web Inc, link this pack.
